summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with fever, altered mental status, and hypoglycemia, found to have MRSA bacteremia from an infected left tunneled hemodialysis catheter. He presented in septic shock requiring pressor support and fluid resuscitation. The infected catheter was removed, and he was started on vancomycin after initial broad-spectrum antibiotics. A temporary femoral dialysis line was placed after a one-week dialysis holiday, followed by a new tunneled right subclavian catheter. His mental status improved, and surveillance cultures remained negative. He experienced a focal seizure due to underdosed Keppra, which was corrected. Knee pain was evaluated and managed as non-infectious effusion. He stabilized on vancomycin, with plans for a six-week course in extended care, and was discharged with updated medications and close monitoring instructions.
problems: Bloodstream infection due to central venous catheter
Localization-related (focal) (partial) epilepsy and epileptic syndromes with simple partial seizures, without mention of intractable epilepsy
